forcedColorsMirroringCheck.myOriginalCheckWasWrong: I asked whether a forced-colors block resets the SURFACE box-shadow without touching a pseudo. That is the wrong question. The keyline now lives ON the pseudo, so the question is whether the PSEUDO's keyline is stripped in forced colors. My check returned 'nothing to mirror' for overlay-modal and dropdown purely because their surfaces carry no shadow reset — which says nothing about the pseudo. This is precisely the instrument failure I have been cataloguing in other lanes all round: my instrument answered a cheaper question than the real one and returned a confident green.

butTheClassIFICATIONdiffers.whatItActuallyIs: A PRE-EXISTING DIVERGENCE from the forced-colors contract that drawer and popover implement: decorative keylines are stripped in the forced palette. Modal and dropdown never stripped theirs. The relocation did not cause it; it made it visible.
butTheClassIFICATIONdiffers.whyThatDistinctionMatters: Fixing modal and dropdown would STRIP A KEYLINE THAT CURRENTLY PAINTS — a paint change, and under FAB-12 an adjudicated visual delta requiring sighted inspection. It is NOT a forward-edit restoration and I will not make it unilaterally. Treating a pre-existing divergence as a regression would have let a real paint change land under a repair label.

No keyline ever painted in the forced palette on any of the four families — not before relocation, not after. My 'no regression / pre-existing divergence' classification for Modal and Dropdown rests entirely on the false premise that their keyline painted there, and is void. It also follows that Drawer's and Popover's explicit `box-shadow: none` resets are REDUNDANT rather than load-bearing, so crediting them as necessary mitigations was also wrong. Direction and contract are referred to the adjudicator and must be settled with a REAL EMULATED CAPTURE, not from the spec text — reading 3.1 and concluding is the same 'by construction' move FAB-11 forbids, which is how I produced the error in the first place.

containingBlockHazard.disposition: CONFIRMED BY ME IN SOURCE, independently of the auditor's report. Line numbers match theirs exactly.
containingBlockHazard.hazard: The relocated keyline pseudos are `position: absolute` and need a positioned ancestor. Three families spread a PUBLIC style prop AFTER the engine sets position, so a caller passing `position: static` re-anchors the pseudo to a different ancestor. The previous INSET shadow painted on the element itself and did not depend on this at all — the hazard is NEW, created by the relocation.

verified.Drawer: EXPOSED. getPositionStyles sets `position: 'fixed'` at the head of `base`, `...style` spreads last in the same object literal.
verified.Popover: PROTECTED. `...overlayStyle` then `...positionStyle` LAST — the engine wins. Useful as a negative control.

containingBlockHazard.reachabilityIsPublic: BaseComponentProps.style is unrestricted CSSProperties; Modal and Drawer extend it; Dropdown's overlayStyle is unrestricted. This is a public API hatch, not an internal one.
containingBlockHazard.containerTypeDoesNotHelp: `container-type: inline-size` on the Dropdown surface does NOT create a containing block for absolute positioning, so it provides no protection.
containingBlockHazard.notFixed: No guard implemented. Referred to the adjudicator with options: narrow the public style type to forbid `position`; merge engine position AFTER the caller's style; give the pseudo a containing block no caller can reach; or declare the hatch out of contract. Requires a Chromium fixture with position:static plus animation:none/reduced-motion, with the two protected branches as controls.
